title: Zipper
content: The zippers that come with CLO3D always seem a bit underwhelming, and their size often appears too small to me. When used on the clothes, they can undermine the overall quality of the garments. That's why I've specifically crafted #5 - sized zippers. There are two types, and each type has two closure methods. All the attributes and adjustment methods of these zippers are fully compatible with the software. I typically apply them to the making of down jackets and padded jackets, which endows the clothing with an overall sense of luxury. I've set up UV grid layouts for both the zippers and their pulls, enabling the customization of LOGOs, just as shown in my illustrations. The UV grids are directly incorporated into the normal map of each zipper file, and the file format is.PSD. After downloading, you can click to make modifications. I'm still in the process of continuous exploration, hoping to offer more convenient methods to enthusiasts!![2430ead84cb140e68e6af7a5a9630abd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/15c014faef94469c93dde357b5fc4cb2/images/2430ead84cb140e68e6af7a5a9630abd%E7%AC%AC%E4%BA%8C%E7%89%88.png)
content_description: This page offers customizable #5-sized zipper assets designed for CLO3D to enhance garment quality and luxury, complete with editable UV grid layouts for personalized logos.

title: How To Remove The Dart On The Trousers Waistline
content:
Tutorial Vidoes show how to draw or shift the dart but they don’t show how to remove the dart.

Can you explain how can I do these pelase?

Step 1) measure the dart base (Let’s say the dart 2 cm)

How to measure the “dart gap” “dart base”?

Step 2) Remove the dart

Step 3) Add 1 cm to each side of the waist line on the Back Trousers Pattern.

Is “Edit Pattern Tool - Offset Pattern Outline” right for this purpose?

![223c5885cc8c4a87830d3a5385f57fbe](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/caa21e06026b4a26ab88fedf375689b3/images/223c5885cc8c4a87830d3a5385f57fbeScreenshot%202026-01-16%20at%2018.46.23.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Just try out the different ideas you have, if it doesn't work you can just revert the last step :) In this case, "Offset Pattern Outline" will affect the entire segment in a parallel way. If you wish to keep a nice curve instead, on suggestion would be to try moving the outer corners via the Edit Pattern tool by dragging. You can open a precision window for measurements by right-clicking at the same time as you are dragging and holding down the left mouse button. Another way would be to right-click on the segment and choose "Change Length", then putting in the desired measurement.
Reply 1: What about Step 2) How do I remove the dart? I could not do this.
Reply 2: Delete the corner point of the dart inside the pattern piece, then smooth out the waistline (two segment points will remain on it, you can covert them to curve points and go from there).
content_description: This webpage explains how to accurately remove a dart from a sewing pattern by measuring the dart base, adjusting the pattern accordingly, and using tools like the "Edit Pattern Tool - Offset Pattern Outline" for precise modifications.

title: How To Measure Dart Gap With The POM Tool
content:
In Segment Mode when I click on the dart leg points It measures the whole dart. (Measurement of the 2 Dart legs)

But I want to measure the distance between those dart legs. (the gap between them on the waist curve)

On the screenshot It is presented as “here”

How can I do this?

![800b92aaf752445782f9ee3f69b05e07](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/dd024be01ff848b8bdfe0b21f18a7b2b/images/800b92aaf752445782f9ee3f69b05e07Screenshot%202026-01-15%20at%2014.54.38.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi there, the POM tool skips empty space as you have noted, but there is a way to trick it into measuring a gap. (1) First, create a random POM on the pattern piece. (2) With the Edit POM tool, grab one end and drag and drop it to one side of the gap - the point will be magnetic and snap to it. (3) Do the same with the other end. The gap is now being measured.
Reply 1: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/dd024be01ff848b8bdfe0b21f18a7b2b some reason the other end of the POM line does not snap to the other edge of the gap.As you see on the screenshot video;???
Reply 2: You still have the entire line selected, not just the point you wish to move. Click in the empty space once to lose the selection, then drag and drop only the point to be moved and it will work :)
Reply 3: Understood. Thank you very much.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on measuring the distance between dart legs on a waist curve using Segment Mode.

Now;Step 1) I create POM in the PolyLine ModeIt shows 0.00Step 2) Switch To The Edit Point Of Measure ToolStep 3) Click onto the yellow dashed line. - Show LengthQuestion 1) At the Object Browser - Point Of Measure sectionIt shows the measure 90.37howeverat the Property Editor - Selected Line Length 48.27?Question 2) I did not grade the pattern.So what is the Length Difference -42.10 here?

So Select just the large middle length you do NOT need > r-click > Select hide length.We do highly recommend testing and trying things out. the best way to sometimes learn CLO is to try the tools and experiment with them..

title: What if Christmas had existed during the Joseon Dynasty?
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/9156cd26a2eb47b59cfbbc11da89210e/images/8d60a4830d1344e888000978acf0b771KakaoTalk_20260111_202309105.jpg)This digital fashion project begins with the imaginary question, “What if Christmas had existed during the Joseon Dynasty?” Rather than directly reproducing Western Christmas imagery, the work envisions a winter festival gently woven into the everyday life and sensibility of Joseon Korea. Through a playful and humorous perspective, it layers contemporary imagination onto the past, suggesting new narrative possibilities in which tradition continues to evolve.

The garment is a knit hanbok created using the latest knit functions of CLO. A variety of knit structures and patterns were applied to express the distinctive construction and silhouette of the hanbok. Traditional Korean floral motifs are rendered as if embroidered through knitting, while the color palette of the Joseon era is reinterpreted in a contemporary manner. By working with the flexible materiality of knit, the design explores the meeting point between the formal language of traditional dress and modern textile sensibilities.

The accessories draw inspiration from traditional Joseon-era adornments such as the jokduri and norigae. The jokduri is reimagined in knit to introduce a soft and tactile quality, while the norigae, traditionally attached to hanbok or bags, is transformed into knit earrings, proposing a new mode of wear. Through these elements, the symbolic and functional aspects of traditional accessories are extended into a contemporary context.

The scene depicts a woman taking a bite of yakgwa, a traditional Korean confection, as she strolls through and lingers in a Joseon-era market and dining space transformed into a Christmas festival. By layering an imagined celebration onto an ordinary moment, the work presents an unfamiliar yet joyful vision of a “Joseon Christmas,” inviting viewers to step into this festive world together.

![5fe943d7832d4977bae63426677717de](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/9156cd26a2eb47b59cfbbc11da89210e/images/5fe943d7832d4977bae63426677717deKakaoTalk_20260111_202309105.jpg)![6d8697a6b5714305a3a8f3b492deeb1a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/9156cd26a2eb47b59cfbbc11da89210e/images/6d8697a6b5714305a3a8f3b492deeb1aKakaoTalk_20260111_202303678.png)![742216b92f83418c8a68c0aeba5bd89f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/9156cd26a2eb47b59cfbbc11da89210e/images/742216b92f83418c8a68c0aeba5bd89f%EB%8B%88%ED%8A%B8%ED%81%B4%EB%A1%9C%EC%A6%88%EC%97%851.webp)

![6026d8c97d91493b93739b57914b8993](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/9156cd26a2eb47b59cfbbc11da89210e/images/6026d8c97d91493b93739b57914b8993%EB%8B%88%ED%8A%B8%20%ED%81%B4%EB%A1%9C%EC%A6%88%EC%97%852.webp)

![13020e2dcd604cc1a5fb4ebf69398e6f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/9156cd26a2eb47b59cfbbc11da89210e/images/13020e2dcd604cc1a5fb4ebf69398e6f%EB%8B%88%ED%8A%B8%20%EC%A0%84%EC%8B%A0.webp)

<https://connect.clo-set.com/ko/detail/1837fdee086b476fb4811c2bc655e390>

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: beautifulllll!!!!😍❤️❤️

Comment 2: This is such a warm and wonderfully imaginative take on Korean heritage. The way you recreated traditional elements like the hanbok, jokduri, and norigae with knit is genius!!!
Reply 1: I worked on this piece while thinking about the Ugly Sweater contest! Since there have been very few works that reinterpret hanbok in knit so far, I thought it would be a fun project. I’m really happy that it turned out exactly that way. Thank you so much for the kind words!
